aria: Animated recap of the Mavericks' 116 to 94 win over Golden State: Cooper Flagg's layup on the break that made it 89 to 60 late in the third quarter, quarter-by-quarter scoring, his 33 points on 11-of-15 shooting with 9 assists, the top scorers, how Dallas won, and Saturday's game against the Clippers.
notes: Box score from the Dallas Mavericks' 116–94 win over the Golden State Warriors at the American Airlines Center on Nov 18, 2026, from the CBS Sports box score, with the line score checked against Bleacher Report and game details from the Associated Press (via CBS Sports), the Dallas Sports Journal, The Ticket and SB Nation's Mavs Moneyball (via Yahoo Sports). All 116 Dallas points and all 94 Golden State points are accounted for, and the quarter scores add up to both totals: Dallas 35–25 after one, 62–49 at the half, 92–72 after three. AP lists Will Richard with 18 points; the CBS box score has 20, which is what makes Golden State's lines add up to 94, so 20 is used. Field goals (42 of 83 to 38 of 89), threes (17 of 41 to 9 of 38), free throws (15 of 19 to 9 of 17), assists (34–28) and steals (11–14) are from the box score. The biggest lead (29) is from AP and the Dallas Sports Journal; Golden State's only lead was 4–3 early in the first quarter and Dallas led for the final 45:49 (Dallas Sports Journal). Flagg's steals differ by source (3 or 4), so they are left out. Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Wednesday's games.

Dallas pulled away from 6–6 with a 19–3 first-quarter run (Dallas Sports Journal) and opened the third quarter with a 16–2 run from 64–51 to 80–53 (Dallas Sports Journal; CBS play-by-play). Flagg had 22 points at the half (Dallas Sports Journal). His layup on the break from Walter Clayton Jr. with 4:01 left in the third made it 89–60 (Dallas Sports Journal; The Ticket; CBS play-by-play). The 17 threes and 34 assists were season highs (Dallas Sports Journal). Dallas snapped a three-game losing streak; Golden State lost its fourth straight, without Stephen Curry (oblique) (AP; Dallas Sports Journal; The Ticket). Dallas hosts the Clippers on Saturday (Yardbarker).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Cooper Flagg's running layup on the break from Walter Clayton Jr. with 4:01 left in the third quarter that made it 89–60, Dallas' biggest lead (Dallas Sports Journal; The Ticket; CBS play-by-play). It is drawn as a drive to the rim. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Dallas Mavericks or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Flagg's listed 6-foot-10 and 205 pounds (Wikipedia), with his arms scaled to the 7-foot wingspan measured at the 2025 NBA Draft Combine (CBS Sports), in Dallas' home white with No. 32 (Wikipedia). He has no approved look on file yet, so he is drawn in the kit with the default skin tone. It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
